text:
kevin: FYI - canary run against mistral-7b-chat (chat_v3 template) just showed a tail latency regression (~1.8x p95->p99) when prompts contain long system messages + dense special-token sequences. I captured a quick flamegraph. Kernel selector flips between 'rope-optimized' and 'byte-fallback' mid-request, which looks like it's thrashing KV cache.

anita: ugh. any traces/links?

kevin: link: https://perf.internal/runs/1955550123 (flame + logs). Repro command I used:
```bash
./run_canary --model mistral-7b-chat --template chat_v3 --prompts=large_system.json --batch=16 --seq=1024 --profile
```
large_system.json includes long policy text + many "[[METADATA]]" tokens (internal format).

miguel: quick q - is tokenizer switching to byte fallback because of non-BMP chars or unknown control bytes in those tokens? That would increase token count and change kernel heuristics.

kevin: yep. token dump shows ~30% of tokens falling back to byte-level encoding for one of the system fields. Token counts jump from ~900 -> ~1500 which forces kernel bin to choose the kernel path that doesn't support our RoPE prefetch optimizations. KV cache ends up getting warmed for the wrong layout and we flush mid-stream.

ben: is this a tokenizer bug or expected behavior with our chat templates? Chat_v3 inserts explicit \u0001 separators which the byte tokenizer classifies as fallback.

sara: also saw duplicated BOS/EOS handling in that template on a couple examples — we append EOS at the end of system and again at the user prefix, so prefix caching sees slightly different prefixes and misses.

miguel: two separate issues then: (1) fallback-triggered kernel switch because tokenization fingerprint changed, (2) prefix mismatch due to template adding extra special tokens -> KV cache fragmentation.

kevin: exactly. profiler shows a pattern: initial kernel choice is rope-optimized (good), then after seeing fallback token types it switches to byte-fallback kernel which has different KV layout. The runtime doesn't reconcile caches across kernel variants so we pay full warmup twice.

anita: can we short-circuit kernel switching mid-request? i.e., choose kernel based on tokenizer fingerprint + max possible token growth for the request before starting.

miguel: that's my preferred fix. We already compute a heuristic for batch size and max sequence length. Add tokenizer_fingerprint -> preferred_kernel mapping and bias selector to keep the initial kernel unless we absolutely need to change.

ben: small note: for some models (llama variants) RoPE scaling means the kernel implemented for shorter sequences is incompatible. We need to ensure kernel binning respects both model.arch and kv/head dims, not only token_type distribution.

kevin: agreed. action plan I propose:
- add a preflight that computes expected token_expansion and tokenizer_fingerprint for the batch before kernel selection (miguel)
- bias kernel selector to choose rope-optimized for Mistral/Mixtral when expected_seq > 512 unless tokenizer fingerprint forces fallback (miguel)
- make prefix canonicalization in chat templates: dedupe BOS/EOS and collapsible separators (anita)
- add a regression test (runtime-ci) with long system prompts + special tokens to catch this (sara)
- canary patch rollout after tests (kevin + deploy-bot)

anita: I'll start with template changes. We can normalize by stripping trailing EOS from system messages and ensuring user prefixes don't re-add them. Quick patch ETA: today EOD.

miguel: I'll add tokenizer_fingerprint to the selector. Plan: compute hash(model_id + tokenizer_version + sample_token_type_histogram) and look up a mapping that prefers kernel_bin. If not found, use current heuristics but with a sticky policy for the duration of the request. ETA: tomorrow morning.

sara: I'll wire a unit/regression that runs the canary used above and asserts p95/p99 within 10% of baseline. runtime-ci will fail the PR if it regresses.

runtime-ci: regression test created: perf/regressions/1955550123-long-system-special-tokens. Triggered on PRs touching selector|tokenizer|templates.

ben: also let's log a small telemetry event when kernel_switch happens mid-request so we can monitor frequency. Include previous_kernel, new_kernel, tokenizer_fingerprint, and kv_cache_evictions_count.

kevin: good call. if we see continued mid-request flips after the fixes, we should consider a more heavyweight approach: merge KV cache layout or add an adapter that allows cache reuse across kernel variants (harder).

anita: re: tokenizer: found root cause for byte fallback: our internal [[METADATA]] uses U+E000 private-use codepoints that the standard tokenizer marks as unknown. Replacing with ASCII-safe separator reduces fallback drastically in my local tests.

miguel: great. two follow-ups for me: (1) update kernel selector mapping for llama/mistral/mixtral/qwen to consider head_dim/kv layout (2) add sticky kernel flag to runtime API so downstream callers can pin if they want.

kevin: assign owners: miguel for selector (PR+canary), anita for templates, sara for tests. I'll coordinate canary and monitor telemetry. I'll open tracking ticket and link in the PRs.

ben: sounds good. i'll add a quick note in product slack — may impact chat templates customers if we change separators, want to give heads-up.

kevin: thanks all. if anyone hits additional weird tokenization combos, drop them here. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: scheduled canary deploy for patch/mid-request-kernel-sticky at 2026-03-19T02:00:00Z (canary pool: 3 nodes).
